entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Girolamo Aleandro was a Venetian humanist, linguist, and cardinal who played a pivotal role in shaping the Catholic Church's response to the Protestant Reformation. As a key figure in the Council of Trent, Aleandro worked tirelessly to promote reform and counter the spread of Protestantism throughout Europe. His efforts ultimately contributed to the development of the Tridentine Mass and the codification of Catholic doctrine.

Born in Venice, Italy around 1519, Aleandro was educated at the University of Padua and later became a member of the Inquisition. He traveled extensively throughout Europe, earning a reputation as a skilled diplomat and strategist. Aleandro's diplomatic efforts were often marked by controversy and conflict, but he remained devoted to his faith and his work in the Church.

Aleandro died on February 11, 1542, in Rome, Italy. His legacy continued to shape the Catholic Church for centuries, influencing the development of Tridentine theology and the Counter-Reformation movement.
